requirements.requirement: Existing data in /srv/inventory owned by user inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc were created (cmd-b632c500fcdd4408), then chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied and directory listing confirms inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership on /srv/inventory, /srv/inventory/data, records.csv, and config.json (cmd-9e6d8e889193400b), reconfirmed post-restart (cmd-af6f2830c3ff44ca).
chmod 750 on directories / 640 on files was applied (cmd-9e6d8e889193400b) and a live test as a group-member user (testreader) successfully read records.csv content (cmd-178d85e035ef4d97).

Live test as a non-member user (testother) returned 'Permission denied' on both cat and ls of the directory/file (cmd-178d85e035ef4d97), consistent with the applied 750/640 mode with no world permissions.

requirements.requirement: Existing contents of /srv/inventory preserved (no data loss/corruption)
requirements.summary: sha256sum of records.csv and config.json captured before any change (cmd-9fb923ebc7814d0f, matching the prepare baseline hashes) and shown identical immediately after chown/chmod (cmd-178d85e035ef4d97) and again after the post-task node restart (cmd-af6f2830c3ff44ca).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 86e223a7... plus healthy ownership/permissions/checksums (cmd-90f4da9e8c4e4e39). Reboot was triggered and acknowledged (cmd-e983a32d2e934e47), connectivity was lost across several polling attempts, then boot_id changed to 63681bec... (cmd-ee61b312214f4cdb), and post-restart state re-verification shows ownership, permissions, checksums, user and group all recovered identically (cmd-af6f2830c3ff44ca). This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — ownership by inventorysvc, group-readability by inventory-readers, inaccessibility to other users, and preservation of existing data — are directly demonstrated through before/after checksums, permission listings, and live access tests as both a group member and a non-member. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently executed on node1, with a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity, and confirmed post-restart recovery of ownership, permissions, checksums, and the created user/group, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good: the only mutations beyond the core fix were two temporary verification users that were promptly removed and a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot mechanism.
limitations: The temp-file /tmp/reboot.log is confirmed present only in the fixed after_executor snapshot; no executor command explicitly removed it, so it is presumed to remain as minor residue.
Command exit code on cmd-178d85e035ef4d97 was 1 (nonzero) due to the expected 'Permission denied' outputs from the intentional negative access test, not a task failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two temporary local users (testreader, testother) were created solely to validate access control (cmd-178d85e035ef4d97) and were removed immediately afterward (cmd-d8a61d01ee5848ed) — a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted verification step directly tied to confirming the group-read/other-deny requirement. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created as the stdout/stderr redirection target for the backgrounded reboot command (cmd-e983a32d2e934e47), was left behind and appears in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; it is small, an expected side effect of the restart mechanism used, and not a security or functional concern, but it was not cleaned up. No failed services, no damaged package state (package-health unchanged: 'U var/lib/chrony/chrony.drift' before and after), and no unnecessary destructive mutations were observed.
